refuted_claims.claim: REPORT.md 'Recorded, not gated' implies that the stop mirror's only residual beyond §9.4 is an unprobed SIGCONT-to-launcher case that 'leaves the child stopped'.
refuted_claims.evidence: Probed. The REPORT omits the more serious consequence. After a mirrored self-stop and `kill -CONT <launcher pid>`, zsh (darwin and Linux) and bash 5.2 (Linux) report the job 'running' while the child stays T indefinitely (transcripts probes/{darwin,linux}/*-transcript-explicit-hp.txt). That is exactly the K6e clause 'never left stopped while the shell believes the job is running'. darwin bash 3.2 still shows 'Stopped'. A separate, undisclosed residual is a launcher hang after a third-party stop/continue of the child (see defects).

Every harness check still passes. But in a non-gated scenario that 3b handled correctly, 3c hangs. A third process sends SIGSTOP (or SIGTSTP) to the child PID, then SIGCONT to the child PID only. The launcher mirrors the stop and stays T forever, and the child is left a zombie. Plain exec and 3b exit 7; 3c never exits until the launcher PID is continued by hand. Reproduced on darwin (both signals) and linux-arm64 (SIGSTOP; SIGTSTP is discarded there because the process group is orphaned). Evidence: review3c/probes/darwin/extstop-src.json, extstop-src3b.json, linux-extra/extstop-3c.json, extstop-3b.json.

defects.description: Liveness regression from the stop mirror, not gated, not disclosed in REPORT.md. Another process (a supervisor, `pkill -STOP/-CONT`, a script) sends SIGSTOP or SIGTSTP to the child PID, then SIGCONT to the child PID only. heimdall-proto has already stopped itself (mirror_child_stop -> kill(getpid())) and nothing continues it, so it never reaps the exited child (left Z) and never exits. A non-interactive parent waits forever. Plain exec and round 3b exit normally (7 in the probe). This is an inherent trade-off of mirroring, and the contract does not rule on third-party stop/continue of the child, so I am escalating rather than deciding. Possible narrowing for the orchestrator to weigh: mirror only when heimdall-proto's process group is the terminal's foreground group or a job-control context; or SIGCONT the child after the self-stop returns (this does not help this case). At minimum it must be recorded in REPORT.md as a residual.
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/runner.rs mirror_child_stop() (kill_process(getpid(), own)) and the run() waitid loop; reproduced by tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-rust/review3c/probes/scripts/extstop.py (darwin: probes/darwin/extstop-src.json vs extstop-src3b.json; linux: probes/linux-extra/extstop-3c.json vs extstop-3b.json)

defects.description: After a mirrored child self-stop, `kill -CONT <heimdall-proto pid>` continues only the launcher. zsh 5.9 (darwin and Linux) and bash 5.2 (Linux) then list the job as Running/running while the child stays T indefinitely (launcher idle, 0 CPU ticks over 2 s, so no spin). This meets the literal K6e clause 'the child is never left stopped while the shell believes the job is running', but it is triggered by an explicit signal to the launcher PID, which §9.4 records as non-gated for TSTP/STOP. Escalate whether SIGCONT falls under that. REPORT.md calls it unprobed and does not say the shell then reports the job running. A cheap remedy: after kill(getpid(), own) returns, send SIGCONT to the child if it is still stopped. That is harmless when the group was already continued.
defects.location: prototypes/rust/src/runner.rs mirror_child_stop(); prototypes/rust/REPORT.md 'Recorded, not gated'; evidence review3c/probes/{darwin,linux}/{bash,zsh}-transcript-explicit-hp.txt

defects.description: Nested job-control child: with `heimdall-proto run -- bash -i`, the child shell moves itself into its own process group (heimdall-proto does not lead the group). After `suspend`, the outer shell now reports the job Stopped, but `fg` continues only heimdall-proto's group. The nested shell stays T while the outer shell believes the job is running, and the terminal is unusable until the nested PID is killed. Plain exec resumes correctly. Not a regression: 3b hung without even a stop notice. This follows from the round-2 shared-group design, and the harness explicitly does not test nested job control. Not disclosed in REPORT.md. Record it for ADR-0002/M01.

summary:
I rebuilt round 3c from a /tmp copy. All four binary digests and the notices digest match dist/manifest.json exactly. I ran harness 2.4.2 against my build on darwin-arm64 and through tests/g02/linux/run.sh (linux-arm64): 139/139 pass on both, exit 0, verified/pass, so no harness check that passed in round 3b regressed. clippy, fmt and cargo test (49/4/28) pass.

My own pty probes, each with a plain-exec control, ran under bash and zsh on both OSes. They confirm the §9.4 K6e self-stop behaviour:
- SIGTSTP, SIGSTOP and SIGTTIN self-stops repeated six times per job, SIGTTOU/SIGTTIN background stops, Ctrl-Z/bg/fg, Ctrl-Z inside the 200 ms grace window (0/110 re-stops), nohup, pipelines and `sh -c` all behave like plain exec. 5x stress per OS showed 0 re-stops.
- K12 closed-stdout parity holds in 81 additional plain/--json pairs, including stderr also closed, fd 1 closed and /dev/full.

The fix report's verdict for the gated criteria is therefore confirmed. I found one undisclosed, non-gated regression:
- A third process stops and then continues the child by PID.
- heimdall-proto mirrors the stop and is never resumed, so it never reaps the child (left a zombie) and never exits.
- Plain exec and round 3b exit normally. Reproduced on darwin (SIGSTOP and SIGTSTP) and Linux (SIGSTOP).

This is an inherent trade-off of mirroring that the contract does not address, so I escalate it rather than decide it (major).

Two minor findings:
- SIGCONT sent only to the launcher after a mirrored stop: zsh and bash 5.2 then show the job running while the child stays stopped. This is the literal K6e clause, triggered by an explicit signal. REPORT.md calls it unprobed.
- A nested job-control shell as the child: fg leaves it stopped. Pre-existing design; not a regression.

Probe caveats:
- The Linux ctrlz_fg_bg 'restopped' flag appears in plain and hp alike; it is a sampling artefact.
- GNU nohup voids the plain nohup scenario on Linux; the nohup_tty variant covers it.
- The jobs regex in the explicit scenario matched the echoed command; the transcripts are authoritative.

Evidence is in <repo>/tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-rust/review3c/ (build/, harness-darwin/, harness-linux/, probes/ with scripts, JSON results and transcripts). The canary/private-key scan is clean. Nothing was committed.
